=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: run_security_pass_inline(), lines 4969-4976 (the `.security_pass_status = "running"` jq write at 4969-4974, followed directly by `post_state_comment || true` at 4975 and `set_tracking_phase_label "ai:security-pass"` at 4976)
  Problem: This is the one security-pass state transition that posts a state comment without calling `reconcile_tracking_body_after_security_pass_transition` first. All eight other transitions this PR touches (fail-closed 4512, terminal 4544, closed-fix 4677, blocked 4830, head-changed 5050, clean 5066, successor adoption 14786, /re-security-pass 15359) reconcile the body between the state write and `post_state_comment`; the `running` write does not.
  Why it fails at runtime: The audit is an LLM-driven pass that runs for minutes. For that entire window the tracking issue body keeps rendering the previous security-pass block — concretely, after the new budget-reset path fires (4907-4915, prior status `passed`), the body still shows `Status: passed` with the old audited SHA while the state comment and label say the pass is running against the new head. That is the exact stale-body condition this PR exists to eliminate (the #3965 incident), just bounded to the audit window plus at most one tick if the runner dies mid-audit. The render reads only state (`render-tracking-body --state-file`), so rendering at `running` produces the accurate `Status: running` / `Audited integration SHA: none` block; the fix is one line inserted between lines 4974 and 4975, identical to the other eight call sites. The PR title promises to "keep the tracking body honest on every security-pass transition", and this transition is the exception.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
  Line or code reference: lines 3659-3661, between `test_security_pass_exhaustion_still_terminalizes_from_blocked_status` (ends line 3657) and `def test_security_pass_terminal_failure_rerenders_tracking_body_security_block` (line 3662)
  Problem: Three consecutive blank lines separate the two top-level test functions. PEP8 E303 allows at most two, and the rest of this file uses two (compare lines 3620-3623).
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — the CI ruff gate (`ruff check --select E,F --ignore E501 scripts/*.py`, ci.yml:335) covers `scripts/*.py` only, so this does not break CI. It is a cosmetic deviation introduced by this diff in a file the PR otherwise conforms to the two-blank-line convention; a one-line deletion fixes it.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: PR body (metadata, not a repo file) — "Proactive fixes included" section: "The seven covered transitions are `passed`, head-changed `pending`, `blocked`, fail-closed, terminal failure, closed-fix failure, and the `/re-security-pass` reset" and the table row "Return transitions that now re-render the body | 7"
  Problem: The implementation and all in-repo docs (README.md 12e, agents.md 458-475, changelog.d/3965-security-pass-cycle-budget-reset.md "Transitions that now re-render the body | 8") now cover eight transitions including stall-recovery successor adoption (added at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14786), but the PR description still says seven and omits successor adoption from the enumerated list.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — but the PR body is the reviewer/operator-facing contract for this change, and it contradicts the merged behavior and the in-repo docs it ships with. `SECURITY_PASS_CYCLE_BUDGET_RESET` itself is correctly registered in both agents.md log-prefix registries and the README env-var rows, and no identifiers were renamed; this is purely stale PR metadata needing a `gh pr edit` body refresh.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
